title: Recurring food-access interruptions at small animal shelters
summary: Test whether intermittent shelter food access is driven by scarcity, matching, transport, freshness, or verification failure before adding new supply.
observed_condition: Illustrative partner reports describe intermittent access to appropriate food while potential donor supply may exist elsewhere.
unresolved_core: Identify the binding constraint and the smallest safe intervention that reduces verified interruptions.
disputes: Interruption frequency still needs a frozen baseline.
Reported donor supply may not be live deployable capacity.
diagnosis: Scarcity is one hypothesis, not the default conclusion.
Matching, transport, timing, verification and food suitability are competing bottlenecks.
knowledge_frontier: Keep nutrition matching species- and condition-specific.
prior_attempts: Ad-hoc donation and volunteer delivery can resolve events without diagnosing recurrence.

capabilities.name: Geospatial routing
capabilities.description: Route candidate pickups under time/distance constraints.
limitations: Does not establish food suitability or live capacity.

capabilities.name: Inventory ingestion
capabilities.description: Normalize item, quantity, timing and donor metadata.
limitations: Stale inventory can create false capacity.

success.falsification: No reduction or increased food-safety incidents

authority: Any field intervention requires explicit approval from participating shelters/operators.

subproblems.title: Establish the baseline
subproblems.detail: Quantify frequency, duration, severity and competing causes.

subproblems.title: Map usable surplus
subproblems.detail: Represent donors, timing and freshness without treating stale inventory as capacity.

subproblems.title: Encode safe compatibility
subproblems.detail: Define species- and condition-aware constraints with expert review.

subproblems.title: Test logistics matching
subproblems.detail: Evaluate routing/scheduling with sandboxed shadow recommendations.

title: Pedestrian conflict around a transit-adjacent intersection
confidence: Verified for research; not yet open
summary: Determine whether a reported crossing conflict is recurrent and which mechanism dominates before proposing infrastructure changes.
observed_condition: Illustrative near-conflict reports suggest avoidable pedestrian/vehicle interaction during peak flows.
unresolved_core: Establish recurrence and distinguish geometry, signal timing, visibility and behavior mechanisms.
disputes: Current reports may be peak-period biased.
A representative exposure denominator is not frozen.
diagnosis: Signal timing, geometry, visibility and behavior remain competing explanations.
knowledge_frontier: Conflict-rate denominator and pre/post measure must be defined.
prior_attempts: Informal observations locate candidates but do not establish intervention effects.

capabilities.name: Video event annotation
capabilities.description: Annotate conflict events from privacy-conscious samples.

capabilities.name: Signal/geometry simulation
capabilities.description: Test competing mechanisms before field changes.

success.target: Independent reviewers can identify mechanism tests and interpretable indicators

authority: Road or signal changes require competent transport authority approval.

evidence.summary: Candidate conflict events reported during peak periods.

subproblems.title: Collect representative observations
subproblems.detail: Sample peak/off-peak periods and estimate exposure.

subproblems.title: Test competing mechanisms
subproblems.detail: Compare timing, geometry, visibility and behavior explanations.

governance_notes: Verification does not authorize infrastructure change.

title: Reproduce a disputed empirical effect with a broader sample
summary: Test whether an empirical relationship survives a preregistered broader-sample replication instead of treating a single specification as settled.
observed_condition: An illustrative published relationship appears sensitive to geography and time window.
unresolved_core: Determine whether the effect survives harmonized measurement and preregistered robustness checks.
disputes: Specification sensitivity may explain apparent disagreement.
diagnosis: Sample composition and measurement harmonization are competing explanations.
knowledge_frontier: Effect direction reported in narrower sample.
prior_attempts: Single-country replication exists but does not resolve broader generalizability.

capabilities.name: Data harmonization
limitations: Source definitions may not fully align.

capabilities.name: Independent replication runner
capabilities.description: Execute frozen protocol from clean environment.

success.target: Independent rerun reproduces the frozen broader-sample result
success.falsification: Result cannot be reproduced or protocol changes after outcome inspection

authority: No consequential intervention; publication claims remain subject to scholarly review.

subproblems.title: Freeze replication protocol
subproblems.detail: Specify estimand, sample, exclusions and robustness family.

subproblems.title: Build harmonized panel
subproblems.detail: Map source definitions and preserve transformation provenance.

subproblems.title: Independent reproduction
subproblems.detail: Execute from a clean environment and compare outputs.

rights_notes: Paper/full-text and datasets retain source-specific rights.
governance_notes: Null and contradictory results remain first-class outcomes.

title: Repeated application abandonment at a documentation step
summary: Test whether a repeated service drop-off reflects documentation/access friction rather than lack of service capacity, without automating eligibility decisions.
observed_condition: An illustrative application funnel shows concentrated abandonment between documentation request and completed submission.
unresolved_core: Determine the causal mix and whether a low-risk information/support intervention reduces avoidable abandonment without changing eligibility rules.
disputes: Some abandonment may be legitimate self-selection.
Administrative delay and documentation gaps can look identical in aggregate data.
diagnosis: The bottleneck may be documentation/access rather than service capacity.
knowledge_frontier: Need transition-level evidence rather than aggregate completion rates.
Support interventions must be separated from eligibility decisions.
prior_attempts: Generic FAQ/reminders improved information availability but did not isolate the binding transition.

capabilities.name: Funnel instrumentation
capabilities.description: Observe transition-level completion without scoring applicant worthiness.

capabilities.name: Document checklist assistant
capabilities.description: Explain required materials without deciding eligibility.

success.target: Improvement without higher incorrect submissions or unacceptable staff burden
success.measurement: Operator funnel plus sampled case review
success.falsification: No improvement or evidence of eligibility/due-process harm

authority: Eligibility, benefits, sanctions or irreversible decisions remain with competent human/institutional authority.

evidence.summary: Concentrated drop-off appears at documentation transition.

subproblems.title: Differentiate abandonment causes
subproblems.detail: Sample cases to distinguish information, documentation, delay, eligibility and deliberate withdrawal.

subproblems.title: Design low-risk support
subproblems.detail: Prototype information/checklist assistance without changing eligibility logic.

subproblems.title: Run shadow comparison
subproblems.detail: Compare support suggestions against frontline decisions and record disagreements.

attempts.summary: Low-risk support prototype accepted for shadow evaluation.

governance_notes: The pilot tests informational support only.

title: Heat-risk resource mapping for outdoor community workers
summary: Demonstrates a problem reaching deployment, outcome observation and resolution while remaining reopenable if the condition returns.
observed_condition: Illustrative outdoor workers reported difficulty finding reliable nearby hydration/cooling resources during high-heat periods.
unresolved_core: At opening, determine whether the binding gap was resource scarcity or discoverability/freshness along work routes.
disputes: Self-reported difficulty did not establish physical scarcity.
Seasonal closures can make apparently available resources unusable.
diagnosis: Discoverability and freshness appeared more important than absolute scarcity in the illustrative pilot.
knowledge_frontier: Resolved packet retains limitations supporting closure and recurrence monitoring.
prior_attempts: Static resource lists became stale and did not reflect hours/temporary closure.

success.falsification: Failure rate unchanged or map directs users to unavailable/unsafe resources

authority: The map provides information; facilities retain authority over access and operating conditions.

evidence.summary: Failed access attempts decreased after freshness-aware mapping in the example pilot.

subproblems.title: Maintain resource freshness
subproblems.detail: Recheck high-use resources before/during high-heat periods.

attempts.summary: Built and verified a freshness-aware resource map.

outcomes.summary: Illustrative pilot recorded fewer failed access attempts.
outcomes.observed_change: Sampled workers reported improved ability to locate verified open resources.

governance_notes: Resolution is reversible; recurrence should reopen rather than erase history.
